question: The application proposes increasing intake from approximately 1.3 million tons per year to 2.6 million wet tons per year (50,000 wet tons/week). What specific emissions, leachate, traffic, and odor modeling has been done at the 2.6M-ton level — not at current levels?

River Birch is currently permitted to accept waste from 13 Louisiana parishes. The application proposes accepting waste from 'all parishes and U.S. states' — i.e., 64 parishes and 50 states. What evidence supports the need for such a dramatic service-area expansion?

River Birch spokesman William Kearney publicly stated (nola.com, 3/22/2026) that accepting out-of-state municipal waste 'is not even a consideration and just completely off the table.' If true, why does the application explicitly request authority to accept waste from all 50 states, and will River Birch withdraw and revise the application to reflect the publicly stated intent?

River Birch's air permit application (EDMS 14829297, page 271) projects annual waste acceptance of exactly 2,066,307 tons each year from 2025 through 2031. How is that flat projection consistent with a solid waste application proposing 2.6M wet tons/year and a 5x expansion of service area?

Surface emissions monitoring data on file (EDMS 15157587) show a methane reading exceeding 434,000 ppm at a surface liner, with 61 areas exceeding 500 ppm in Q3 2025 and 47 areas exceeding 500 ppm in Q4 2025. What is the root cause of these exceedances and what corrective action has been taken?

The adjacent Jefferson Parish (Kelvin) Landfill has not accepted waste since August 2023 and will not resume until 2027 — meaning it cannot account for the methane signal. Has LDEQ independently confirmed that the methane plume observed in carbon-mapper.org data over this site is attributable to River Birch?
Given current, documented methane exceedances at hundreds of points across multiple quarters, what is the technical basis for concluding that doubling intake will not worsen these emissions?

LAC 33:VII.709.5 requires a description of total existing land use within 3 miles. This description was NOT submitted with the major modification application. Why was the application deemed technically complete on 12/5/2025 in the absence of this required element?

The LDOTD letter dated 10/17/2025 (Bao Long Le, P.E.) states only that LDOTD has 'no objections to the continued operation of the landfill.' The previous LDOTD evaluation was conducted 2/12/2018. Has LDOTD been informed that the application proposes doubling intake and a 5x service-area expansion, and is LDOTD's concurrence based on that updated scope?

The 2018 traffic study predates the Live Oak subdivision (250 homes, built 2021–present) and the Water Oaks subdivision (200 homesites currently in development, 1,500 feet from the River Birch property line). Will LDEQ require a new traffic impact study that includes these subdivisions and the proposed entrance at Live Oak and South Kenner Avenue?

Will the modified permit require River Birch to fund dust mitigation, truck-washing stations, and road maintenance on US 90, Live Oak, and South Kenner Avenue commensurate with the projected truck volume?

The application does not describe how waste from 'all parishes and U.S. states' would actually be transported (truck, rail, barge, or combination). Will River Birch be required to specify transport modes, quantify tonnage by mode, and address emissions at every transfer point — including rail-car unloading?
If rail transport is contemplated, what is the planned rail route and what are the air-quality, noise, and odor impacts along the Huey P. Long bridge corridor and adjacent neighborhoods?

The current Odor Management Plan (EDMS 14919015) is the subject of numerous odor complaints. Why is this plan being relied on for an application that proposes doubling intake and accepting longer-aged waste from out of state?

The Inclement Weather Procedures (EDMS 14919015, Section 2.5) do not address a Katrina-scale event that renders the New Orleans area uninhabitable for weeks or months. If River Birch is accepting waste from all 50 states, what is the plan when the host community cannot staff or access the facility?

The River Birch site is located along the north-south flightpath of Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY). A February 10, 2026 Times-Picayune photo of land slated for River Birch expansion shows a large concentration of birds. What is the documented bird-strike risk and what bird-deterrence program is in place, beyond simple distance from runway threshold?

In 1995, the FAA and the New Orleans International Airport formally objected to the original River Birch landfill on bird-strike grounds (FAA Order 5200.5A). Have the FAA and the MSY airport operator been formally re-consulted on this major modification, and are their current responses in the record?

The proposed modification incorporates the adjacent Greater New Orleans Landfill into the River Birch footprint. What is the closure/cap status of the GNOL footprint, and how will historical contamination, leachate, and gas from GNOL be addressed under the combined permit?

The 1996 denial letter (Secretary Kucharski, EDMS 279821) specifically noted that River Birch was 'contiguous to the Greater New Orleans Landfill' and to the Kelvin Landfill, with at least seven other landfills within five miles, and concluded that 'a disproportionate burden has been borne by adjacent communities.' What has materially changed in the past 30 years that would justify a different conclusion now?

The application adds Type III C&D debris acceptance. What is the projected C&D tonnage, where will it be placed within the footprint, and how will asbestos-containing materials, treated wood, and other regulated C&D components be screened and managed?

River Birch requests use of a geomembrane-supported geosynthetic clay liner in lieu of the standard liner or the previously-approved alternative. Has the technical demonstration been independently reviewed, and how does the alternative liner perform under the increased leachate head expected at 2.6M wet tons/year?

The Fact Sheet discloses three solid-waste enforcement actions and two multi-media enforcement actions in the past four years, including SE-CN-22-003414 (monitoring well construction, cover application, unauthorized waste), MM-CN-23-002255 (leachate migration), SE-N-24-002896 (failure to notify of a fire), and settlement SA-MM-25-00518 (issued 11/13/2025). What permanent corrective actions have been taken for each, and what is the current verified compliance status?
Notice of Violation SE-N-24-00289 was returned as 'lost in transit' by USPS. Has River Birch since been served with this NOV, and what is its status?
What was the cause of the January 2025 fire at the facility (SE-N-24-002896), and what fire-prevention measures have been added to the operations plan as a result?

The Kean Miller LLP letter dated 4/7/2025 asserts that proposed future projects 'will serve and benefit Jefferson and St. Charles parishes,' but provides no supporting evidence. What specific, enforceable benefits to Jefferson and St. Charles parishes are tied to permit approval, and are any of them contingent on the major modification (as opposed to projects River Birch could undertake under the existing permit)?
River Birch is a privately-owned and operated facility. What enforceable host-community benefit agreement (tipping-fee surcharge, road fund, health monitoring fund) is included as a permit condition?

The original River Birch Landfill permit application was DENIED on 1/8/1996 by Secretary William A. Kucharski (EDMS 279821) on the explicit basis that 'a disproportionate burden has been borne by adjacent communities' and that there was no 'clear and planned benefit to the state, at large.' Has LDEQ analyzed how, if at all, the public-interest balancing differs in 2026 — given that the area has only become more developed and more burdened in the intervening 30 years?

The Jefferson Parish Zoning Appeals Board formally opposed the original River Birch permit in 1995 on zoning, alternative-site, and aviation grounds. What is the current formal position of the Jefferson Parish Council on the proposed major modification, and is it in the record (per EDMS 15150229)?

The 1996 denial decision stated there were 'over 5,000 residents within one and one-half miles of the proposed facility.' What is the current population within 1, 1.5, 3, and 5 miles given the development of Live Oak, Water Oaks, and other subdivisions since 1996?

Attachment 56 of the application contains a Capacity Evaluation. Does that evaluation account for the doubled intake (2.6M wet tons/year) over the projected life of the facility, and what is the resulting remaining airspace and closure date?

The public hearing was held 4/21/2026 at the James C. Simmons Community Center. Were copies of the application made available at additional public locations beyond the Avondale branch library, Jefferson Parish Council, and LDEQ Southeast Regional office — given that the proposed service area covers all 64 parishes?

What demonstrated need for additional generating capacity within St. Charles Parish (as opposed to elsewhere on the grid) does the application establish, given that the parish already produces roughly 20 times the electricity it consumes and its population has declined since 2010?

If the generation is intended to serve a data-center load located in Richland Parish, does the EAS justify siting the emissions in St. Charles Parish, and were lower-burden alternative sites evaluated?
Does the cumulative analysis account for the existing Waterford 3 nuclear station, Waterford 1 & 2, and the neighboring petrochemical facilities as co-located or commonly affecting sources?

Does the application disclose all enforcement actions, notices of violation, and consent decrees at Entergy's other Louisiana generating facilities within the past 5 years, and what corrective actions resulted?
If these units displace or defer retirement decisions for Waterford 1 & 2, does the application net out those emissions, or does it present Waterford 5 & 6 as wholly new load?
Is there a site-wide cleanup and redevelopment plan addressing how Waterford 5 & 6 decommissioning interacts with Waterford 3 and the legacy units?

Section 1 (Site Characterization, p.98 ToC / Table 1-21) lists "Orphan Wells Within 5 Miles of the Proposed Project Location," yet Section 3 (AOR and Corrective Action Plan) states no artificial penetrations exist in the Area of Review and concludes no corrective action plan is needed. Does the AOR search radius match the 5-mile radius used for Table 1-21, does it cover the pressure front (not just the CO2 plume), and do any Table 1-21 wells fall within the actual AOR boundary?

The Plume Model (Section 2) states the pressure/plume model domain covers approximately 47,100 acres (~74 sq mi), while the state lease and Site Characterization both give the controlled acreage as 21,079.18 acres. For the roughly 26,000 acres of modeled pressure-front extent that fall outside the leased/controlled acreage, what pore-space rights, notice, or consent has the applicant obtained from those other owners, and how does the application's repeated assertion that "the CO2 plume growth and extent will remain on the acreage controlled by" the applicant account for the pressure front rather than only the free-phase plume?

ERRP Section 8 redacts pages 6-11 of 15 -- the pages containing the full narrative for all 8 identified risk scenarios (including Single Large-Volume CO2 Release to the Surface, Well Blowout, and Loss of Mechanical Integrity) and the risk matrix scoring referenced at Appendix G-1. What specific statutory exemption (trade secret, critical infrastructure security, or other) is claimed for withholding the risk-scenario narratives themselves -- as opposed to withholding genuinely sensitive details like exact coordinates or security countermeasures -- and how can the public meaningfully comment on emergency-response adequacy for a wetland WMA site without access to the risk scenarios being planned for?

Financial Assurance Section 9 states the funding mechanism is Bond for "Injection and Monitoring Well Plugging" but Insurance for both "Post-Injection Site Care and Site Closure" and "Emergency and Remedial Response" -- and the pages containing every dollar figure are redacted. Insurance is a claims-made/eligibility-dependent instrument rather than a pre-funded, draw-on-demand instrument like a bond or trust. What is the actual dollar amount of coverage for PISC/site closure and for emergency/remedial response, what is the policy term relative to the decades-long PISC obligation, and why was insurance chosen over a bond or trust for these specific cost categories given Class VI's emphasis on assured, immediately available closure funding?

QASP (Quality Assurance and Surveillance Plan) redacts roughly half its pages, concentrated in the sections covering monitoring instrumentation, corrosion monitoring, CO2 stream analysis, and groundwater sampling and analysis protocols. What specific instrumentation, detection limits, and sampling frequencies are proposed for mechanical integrity and groundwater monitoring, and on what basis are these methodological details -- as opposed to any genuinely proprietary instrument specifications -- withheld from public review of a program's ability to detect a leak before it reaches a USDW?
